title: Compass momentum check: mid-cycle notes
content:
Purpose: quick, portable packet for my manager sync — surface momentum, friction, and a small set of asks. Keep this short, evidence-first.

Headline ask (one line): can I get alignment to run a focused growth experiment (0.2F recruiter + 4 weeks interview pipeline) to validate a senior IC promotion for Q3?

Why now (context):
- Strong signal from last 6 weeks: two cross-team projects shipped where I led hiring coordination + onboarding tweaks. Both had measurable drop in time-to-productivity.
- Business context: product onboarding velocity directly tied to gross retention metrics in our mid-market cohort (see linked confluence note).

Top-line evidence (short bullets):
- Onboarding velocity: cohort onboard time (feature-activation) median moved from ~7 days -> ~4 days for hires I shadowed (sample n=9, Oct–Dec). Quick wins I ran: pre-day kit, role-aligned pairing, triage checklist.
- Quality signals: peer feedback summary: 8/9 hires scored >= 4/5 on first-sprint deliverables.
- Product impact hypothesis (qualitative): reduced friction in onboarding likely explains part of +3% weekly retention uplift in small pilot customers. Need analytics team to attribute.

Risks/unknowns:
- Sample size small; selection bias (hired into healthy teams).
- Hiring market realities — timing for recruiter bandwidth and approval.
- Promotion timeline constraints vs. calibration cycle.

Ask breakdown (concrete, labeled):
- A1: Approval for 0.2F dedicated recruiter time for 4–6 weeks to run a scoped search and validate senior IC hire (metrics: 10 screens, 3 on-site/loop, 1 hire).
- A2: Sponsor time: 2 hours for calibration + decision commit at end of experiment window.
- A3: Access to product retention slices + permission for me to pair with analytics for attribution (JIRA OPS-4321).

Manager prep notes (what I want from manager in the meeting):
- Quick gut-check on timing (is Q3 runway feasible?).
- Feedback on framing the promotion case (bias checks I should include).
- Commitment on calibration meeting date (target: 2026-03-15).

Signals I will surface if experiment is successful (decision criteria):
- Hire demonstrates ramp-to-deliver within 6 weeks on onboarding metric equivalent to prior sample (median <= 5 days).
- Manager+peer scoring >= 4/5 for first two sprints.
- Direct measurable improvement (>=2 percentage points) in trial customer retention cohort where new onboarding flows were applied.

Mini action plan (next 6 weeks):
- Week 0: finalize role spec + interview rubric (owner: me).
- Week 1–3: recruiter screens + initial loops (owner: recruiter + me).
- Week 4: final loops + calibration (owner: hiring manager + me).
- Week 5–6: offer + onboard (if successful) and run first-ramp measurement.

Notes to self (bullet reminders, rough):
- When making promotion ask, frame impact in customer retention terms — that resonates with exec team.
- Bring 2 counterfactuals: if we don’t hire, what fails? (List 3 scenarios).
- Preempt compensation questions: have market comp comps ready (export from compensation sheet).

Open questions (to tidy before meeting):
- Can we get analytics help to instrument the onboarding retention test? (who is the contact?)
- Is 0.2F recruiter realistic for the next hire window?
- How to handle backfill if hire moves from IC to a leadership-y role quickly?

Quick references (to link in the meeting):
- Confluence: Compass framework + promotion rubric (linked in metadata).
- JIRA: OPS-4321 (analytics gating).
- PR: people-ops/pull/212 (small onboarding kit changes deployed).

Tone cue for meeting: start with the shortest headline, then 2 evidence bullets, then the ask. Avoid long history unless manager asks. End with one concrete next step and proposed date.

Scratch ideas (brainstorm, not for meeting unless asked):
- Small experiment: dedicated "onboarding sprint" day where new hires pairbook with senior devs — measure time to first PR.
- Short internal playbook: 1-page checklist that product managers sign off on before new hires begin (reduces first-week blockers).

End of file.
